owned_session_identity.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): the uuid is minted by the adapter and passed as --session-id, so the coordinator knows the id before the process starts; the runtime echoes it on every record and rejects a non-uuid before starting. `--session-id` cannot be combined with `--resume` unless `--fork-session` is given, so a plain resume passes only `--resume <id>` and the conversation keeps the minted id

observed_cancellation.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin), re-run 7 September 2026 with the machine signed in through claude.ai (17 of 17 checks passed, none skipped): the interrupt control round-trip is answered with a control_response carrying still_queued, and interrupting a RUNNING model turn produced a receipt in state observed behind a turn_interrupted terminal record; process-group termination leaves the group empty (SIGTERM ended the process with exit 143). The earlier record said this could not be executed because the stored OAuth session was expired; that reading of the runtime's account block was wrong.

resume_session.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin), re-run 7 September 2026 with the machine signed in through claude.ai (17 of 17 checks passed, none skipped): `--resume <id>` reuses the id in a fresh process; `--resume <old> --fork-session --session-id <new>` mints the new id; an unknown id yields a bare `No conversation found with session ID: ...` line plus a result record with subtype error_during_execution. Executed end to end: a first turn was asked to remember a random word, its process was stopped, and the resumed turn in a new process answered from the earlier turn's history.

active_turn_delivery.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin), re-run 7 September 2026 with the machine signed in through claude.ai (17 of 17 checks passed, none skipped): a user message written to the live process's stdin during a RUNNING model turn is acknowledged by the runtime (--replay-user-messages echoes it with isReplay=true). What is still not established is whether the runtime injects it into that running turn or schedules it as the next one: the runtime reports no field that distinguishes them, and its own queued_turn_count / still_queued describe a queue. The adapter therefore reports submitted_to_active_turn only when active_turn_delivery is verified, and queued with holder runtime otherwise.

sandbox_workspace_write.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin) (FR042): Claude Code 2.1.260 has NO OS sandbox. Executed proof: a SessionStart hook the runtime itself launched wrote outside every --add-dir directory, wrote to /tmp, read a file outside them and reached https://example.com (HTTP 200) — identically with and without `--restricted --permission-mode plan --permission-prompts none`. What the flags do bound is the TOOL SURFACE offered to the model, which is verified (`--restricted --tools Read Glob Grep` yields exactly Glob, Grep, Read; adding Edit and Write yields exactly those five; no Bash, no Task, no WebFetch, no MCP server). That is a permission boundary, not a containment boundary, so the plan's local-development profile cannot be enforced by this runtime and a kernel-level boundary must come from the environment around the process. Separately: without `--setting-sources ''` a registered project's own .claude/settings.json SessionStart hook RAN host commands in the worker session; the adapter always passes it and the hook then did not run

model_selection.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): the `initialize` control response lists the models the runtime offers with their resolved ids and supported effort levels (default, opus[1m], claude-fable-5-1[1m], sonnet, haiku on this machine); `--model sonnet` was reflected in the session's init record as claude-sonnet-5. No model turn is needed for either

effort_selection.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin): `--effort` is accepted and the runtime lists low, medium, high, xhigh, max per model in the initialize control response. An unknown value prints `Warning: Unknown --effort value ... ignoring it and using the default effort` and continues, so the adapter refuses one before spawning rather than letting it be silently mapped. The runtime never reports the EFFECTIVE effort back in any record, so what actually took effect cannot be recorded

token_usage_report.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin), re-run 7 September 2026 with the machine signed in through claude.ai (17 of 17 checks passed, none skipped): the result record carries usage (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens) and modelUsage, and real turns reported non-zero counts. The earlier record claimed every turn failed authentication before reaching the provider so that only zeros were ever observed; that was true of one afternoon's machine state, not of this runtime.

cost_report.note: WP05 tests/adapters/claude-code/real-runtime.test.ts (claude 2.1.260, darwin), re-run 7 September 2026 with the machine signed in through claude.ai (17 of 17 checks passed, none skipped): unlike Codex, the result record carries total_cost_usd, and a real turn reported a measured 0.0369615, and a coordinator run of the ts-bug task reported 10/1644 tokens at 0.0533808. The adapter reports cost as measured only when duration_api_ms > 0 or a non-zero token count is present, and as unavailable with a reason otherwise - never zero for unknown.
